Vanessa / Marissa — reviewed Elliot's traces and the SLO sheet. Below is a pragmatic config to get to p95 ~300ms in the streaming path and a rough cost sketch. This is a first-pass; we should benchmark on the recommended model variants.

Recommended serving config (streaming, interactive chat):
- Dedicated low-latency fleet (routed by policy) using A100-40GB equiv.
- Micro-batching 8 for incoming chunks; continuous batching layer internally to aggregate small chunks while preserving streaming commitments. This keeps per-chunk overhead low and allows high GPU utilization.
- KV cache: keep session KV in local GPU memory with TTL 45 minutes; shard by user-session for fast lookups.
- Quantization: start with q4_k_mixed for the primary variant; keep q8_fallback for critical clinician queries.
- Model variants: primary open-llm-large-16k-quant (quant profile above), fallback open-llm-medium-8k. Use automatic fallback when queueing exceeds 200ms extra latency.

Ops notes & risks:
- Autoscaling warmup: reserve a small buffer of always-on capacity (~10–15% of steady steady load) to avoid cold-starts during bursts. Cold-start GPU instance spin-up can be 45–90s — unacceptable for interactive spikes.
- For predictable bursts (e.g., shift changes), recommend schedule-based pre-warming.
- Telemetry: we must disable any outbound model telemetry and ensure keys stay in customer KMS.

Rough capacity & cost delta (very rough, depends on final perf runs):
- Steady-state (200 rps, median session): estimated 6–8 A100-equivalent GPUs for the streaming fleet.
- Burst headroom to 500 rps (2–5 min): need an additional 8–10 hot GPUs (or higher packing efficiency with 2x micro-batching) to avoid queueing.
- Cost impact: compute spend during bursts could increase by ~30–45% above steady-state for those minutes. Amortized over the month (assuming 1 hour/day of burst-like behavior), blended cost increase ~6–10%.

Follow-ups I need from the customer to firm numbers:
- A few more representative traces or a short replay load (we can run through our perf lab).
- Confirmation on maximum tolerated queueing (e.g., 50ms vs 200ms) and whether some endpoints can use a higher-latency path.

If you want, I can pull a sample perf run on open-llm-large-16k-quant this week and give a concrete tokens/sec and latency curve.
